facts.fact: Prince Udai walked the princes' way in winter with an unnamed guest sixty winters ago, 'the year before the Closing Law was written' in the old women's reckoning. Ila goes still at the number and says only that she is counting; Kunal takes it for arithmetic.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires the family story, and a date makes the guest a clue (C06) the reader can connect to Ila's grandfather (F041) before either lead does.

facts.fact: Raghu's men dug nine holes round the toppled door cairn and turned its base stone face down, hunting a carved marker. Their tracks, two loaded pairs, follow the north-east fork, which runs along the rim shelf toward the Kuhl cut and a shoulder overlooking the head of the Glass Lakes. The left fork curves round the bowl's lip and adds about half a day.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Kunal lead Ila the long way round away from Raghu's tracks and the east fork.

facts.fact: The princes' way has no carved marker; Kunal states the cairn never bore one. Ila writes the words 'Glass Lakes' in her field book with no bearing, and tells Kunal she will ask for a bearing later and will mark any refusal.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Kunal name the lakes aloud and Ila record it openly.
